title: How great product teams prioritize
transcript: Great product teams make explicit choices about what they will not build. Prioritization requires understanding the customer problem, expected impact, confidence, and the effort required. A useful product team does not simply create a longer roadmap. It creates clarity around which problems matter most.

title: Growth experiments that actually teach you something
transcript: A good growth experiment starts with a clear hypothesis. Teams should define what they expect to happen before launching the experiment. The goal is not merely to produce a positive metric. The goal is to learn whether the underlying assumption is supported by evidence.
